title: Slim down model ingest pipeline: consolidate weight providers and migrate tokenizer to proxy stub
creator: Sana Iyer
description:
Objective: Reduce complexity and runtime overhead in the model ingest pipeline by consolidating multiple weight format adapters into a single provider registry, introducing a lazy memory-mapped weight loader, and decoupling tokenizer integration behind a lightweight RPC proxy stub. This ticket targets three failure modes we see in production: long cold-start deserialization, high peak memory due to duplicate weight copies during conversion, and brittle tokenizer handoffs between platform and model adapters.

Scope: - Replace ad-hoc per-format loader implementations with a provider registry that detects formats and selects a single normalized ingestion path. - Add a lazy mmap-based ephemeral view for weight segments to avoid eager full copies on load. - Introduce a tokenizer-proxy process (local RPC) so model bootstrap can treat tokenization as a dependency instead of inlined library calls; the proxy will serve tokenization contract v1 and a compat shim for legacy v0 checkpoints. - Preserve runtime fallback: if mmap is unavailable (e.g., windows/offloaded FS), fall back to current loader path. - Add end-to-end benchmarks and upgrade path for existing checkpoint manifests.

Non-Goals: changing on-disk checkpoint formats, altering KV cache runtime semantics, or removing support for any customer checkpoint format in a single release.
acceptance_criteria: Single provider registry implemented with unit tests covering format detection (hf, ckpt, custom) and selection logic
Lazy-mmap loader reduces peak resident memory for cold model load by >=20% in CI benchmark compared to baseline (measured on p4d-24)
Tokenizer proxy v1 implemented with a gRPC/Unix-socket local transport and compatibility shim for v0 tokenizers
No change in inference correctness for existing regression tests (tokenization parity, logits within numerical tolerance)
Migration script that rewrites manifest pointers for legacy checkpoints is available and validated on internal sample corpora
Feature flags added to toggle new loader and tokenizer proxy for canary rollout

notes: We chose mmap semantics to avoid double-buffering during weight decoding; implementation uses posix_madvise and a small copy-on-write path for layers that need in-place mutation.
Provider registry will be a thin table of detectors -> loader funcs. New loaders must opt into zero-copy where possible; legacy loaders are wrapped in a shim that marks them as 'eager'.

Tokenizer proxy reduces coupling with Python tokenizers in the runtime; will ship as a small Rust binary exposing a minimal RPC schema. This reduces memory overhead and avoids embedding large pip deps into the runtime container.
We will not remove any format adapters in this release; instead mark legacy adapters as deprecated and add telemetry to measure usage before removal.
benchmarks: With mmap loader (prototype): resident 6.8GB, time 15.6s (-26% memory, -15% time)
Throughput unchanged for steady-state generation at 2048 tokens/min; slight CPU increase during first 2 layers due to posix_fadvise overhead
Tokenization latency via proxy: +0.4ms median per token vs in-process on same host; acceptable for our latency SLOs when used with batching
